title: Abliterated models on LiteLLM | liteLLM
summary: Call abliterated models from Refuseless and Abliteration through LiteLLM, with gateway access controls, streaming, tool calls, and cached-token pricing.
body_markdown:
## What is an abliterated model?


Abliteration modifies the weights of an open-weight model to reduce its learned refusal behavior. Developers identify directions in the model's internal representations associated with refusal, then suppress those directions.


[Arditi and colleagues demonstrated this in 13 chat models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11717) in 2024. Hosted providers may use different methods. Reducing refusals can also change answer quality, so evaluate the modified model on the tasks you want it to perform.


You can use these models for security research, red-teaming, and other workflows where a standard chat model refuses prompts you need to explore. The provider hosts the modified weights; LiteLLM connects your application to its API.
